newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Elec raises 64MB DRAM output plan.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Elec raises 64MB DRAM output plan.

text.p: Mitsubishi Electric Corp said on Tuesday that it had raised its planned production for 64-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips and flash memory chips.
Mitsubishi has revised up its production plans for 64-megabit DRAM chips to two million chips a month by the end of 1997 from its previous target of one million a month, a company spokesman said.
It has raised its planned output for flash memory chips to two million a month in the year from April 1, 1997, from its previous plan of one million a month, the company said in a statement.
Mitsubishi will invest about 20 billion yen on equipment at its plant in Kumamoto Prefecture in western Japan to increase output of 64-megabit DRAM chips, the spokesman said.
The revision in the production plan was due to robust demand for 64-megabit DRAMs used in workstations and servers, he said.
The company started making 64-megabit DRAMs at a monthly pace of 50,000 chips per month in late 1996 at its research facility in Hyogo Prefecture, also in western Japan, he said.
It will increase monthly output to 300,000 to 400,000 chips around March and to one million in July, the spokesman said.
He also said Mitsubishi decided to boost production of 64-megabit DRAM chips instead of 16-megabit DRAMs as increased production of 16-megabit DRAMs could lead to an oversupply in the market.
Mitsubishi will maintain its plan to produce 16-megabit DRAM chips, currently the most popular ones used in the industry, at a monthly pace of 10 million chips, the statement said.
But it will reduce output of 16-megabit DRAMs at its Kumamoto plant where Mitsubishi plans to produce 64-megabit DRAMs, the statement said.

The decline in production at the Kumamoto plant will be covered by an increase in output at Powerchip Semiconductor Inc, Mitsubishi's joint venture in Taiwan, and production at its European plant, the statement said.
